test_title: PYST 2: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: maths
question: If an article is sold for Rs. 355, there is a loss of 29%. At what price (in Rs.) should it be sold to gain 31% of profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 29% → Selling Price = 100% − 29% = 71%

Gain of 31% → Selling Price = 100% + 31% = 131%

According to the question, 71% → ₹355

Required Selling Price = (355 ÷ 71) × 131 = 5 × 131 = ₹655

**∴ The correct answer is ₹655.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹355, Loss = 29%, Target Profit = 31%

**Formula Used:** Cost Price (CP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]; New SP = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a4c6a6559502e9f513fcad97d011a6d66ddc84d77912940416b7794b83c32d4c.png] 

⇒ 71% of CP = ₹355

⇒ CP = (355 ÷ 71) × 100

⇒ CP = 5 × 100 = ₹500

⇒ Target Selling Price (SP₂) = 500 × (100 + 31) ÷ 100

⇒ SP₂ = 5 × 131

⇒ SP₂ = ₹655

**∴ The correct answer is ₹655.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base of CP

Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless mentioned otherwise. CP is always considered as 100%.

Direct Ratio Method

When CP is constant, SP₁ ÷ (100 − L₁%) = SP₂ ÷ (100 + P₂%). This allows solving for a new selling price in a single step.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).
